entries.title: Psalms 44:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: My king - The whole people speak as one man, being united in one body.

entries.title: Psalms 44:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Scattered - Those who were not slain are carried into captivity, and dispersed in several places.

entries.title: Psalms 44:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Avenger - Who executeth both God's and his own vengeance upon me.

entries.title: Psalms 44:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Yet - Although we cannot excuse ourselves from many other sins, yet through thy grace we have kept ourselves from apostacy and idolatry, notwithstanding all examples and provocations.

entries.title: Psalms 44:19
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Broken us - By inflicting upon us one breach after another, thou hast at last brought us to this pass. The place - A place extremely desolate, such as dragons love, Isa 13:21,22, and therefore full of horror, and danger. Covered us - With deadly horrors and miseries.

entries.title: Psalms 44:22
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Yea - Because we are constant in thy worship, which they abhor.

entries.title: Psalms 44:25
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Our soul - Our persons. Our belly - We are not only thrown down to the earth, but we lie there like dead carcases.
